title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 94–95). X is a hyperbolic ('anabélienne') curve over a field K, with Γ = Gal(K̄/K). 𝒞 = Π̂₁(X, I) is the profinite fundamental groupoid with a set of base points I ⊂ X(K̄). Page 94 lists two necessary conditions for an automorphism Θ of 𝒞, trivial on objects, to come from some u ∈ Γ:
- (a) Lifting to covers: for every finite étale cover X' → X defined over K, Θ lifts to an automorphism Θ̃ of Π̂₁(X', I'), where I' = X'|I, and Θ̃ is the identity on I' ∩ X'(K).
- (b) Compatibility with maps to hyperbolic curves: for every map f: X' → Y to a hyperbolic curve Y over K, and every x' ∈ I' ∩ X'(K), the image of π̂₁(X', x') → π̂₁(Y, f(x')) is stable under Θ̃ (for a suitable Θ̃). More generally, for a non-rational x', take ν with Θ^ν x' = x' and require stability under Θ^ν.

This page (reading the image) continues roughly: 'I think it is not too unreasonable to conjecture that these conditions are [sufficiently] draconian … to imply that Θ does come from some u ∈ Γ, when X is (say) an anabelian algebraic curve and K is a finitely generated extension of Q.' 'Courbe algébrique anabélienne' is underlined.

So the conjecture is a Galois-image characterization for a single curve. Γ ↪ Aut of the tower of fundamental groupoids of X and its covers, and the image is cut out by two kinds of combinatorial data:
- the 'rational points' of every cover, i.e. the Galois-fixed base points / sections;
- the 'geometric' subgroups coming from all morphisms to other hyperbolic curves.

Uniqueness of u:
- When K is algebraic over Q, Grothendieck expects u to be unique, i.e. the outer Galois representation is faithful.
- When trdeg K > 0, uniqueness requires at least that the field of moduli of X has the same transcendence degree, i.e. that K is finite over the field of moduli. Otherwise X descends to a subfield K₀ over which K is transcendental, and Gal(K̄/K·K̄₀) acts trivially.
- He does not know whether uniqueness then holds.

He then returns to a technical lemma: lifting an automorphism Θ of a groupoid like 𝒞 to a covering groupoid 𝒞̃ when Θ fixes a vertex. Page 96 drops connectedness of 𝒞̃: covers that are only K-connected, studied via stabilizer maps into conjugacy classes of subgroups.

The diagonal margin is largely illegible. It appears to question whether condition b) is really needed or follows from a), and it seems to mention Belyi and 'les conditions algébriques … absolument'. The Belyi mention plausibly concerns maps to P¹ − {0,1,∞}, which would tie condition b) to the Teichmüller/GT-type characterization.
errors: The necessity claim for uniqueness is correct. If K is not finite over the field of moduli, then (after a finite extension) X descends to a subfield K₀ ⊂ K with trdeg(K/K₀) > 0, and the nontrivial group Gal(K̄/K·K̄₀) acts trivially on the geometric π₁. The field-of-moduli versus field-of-definition subtlety is harmless up to finite extension.
The sufficiency conjecture is stated without proof, as a conjecture. No errors in the reasoning shown; the margin is too illegible to check.

ideas.what: Conjecture: for an anabelian curve X over a field K finitely generated over Q, an automorphism of the profinite fundamental groupoid that (a) lifts to all finite étale covers fixing their K-rational base points and (b) preserves images of π₁ under all maps to hyperbolic curves comes from a unique element of Gal(K̄/K).
ideas.modern_name: Galois-image characterization of G_K in Out(π₁) / curve-wise analogue of the Ihara–Oda–Matsumoto (I/OM) conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (question, 1980s); Oda–Matsumoto (conjecture, early 1990s); Pop (proofs of versions, 2010s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and the 1983 letter to Faltings discuss anabelian geometry and Galois actions on Teichmüller towers. This specific single-curve formulation with conditions (a)–(b) is not known to be there (unsure).

ideas.what: Faithfulness of the outer Galois action for hyperbolic curves over algebraic K; over transcendental K, faithfulness requires K to be finite over the field of moduli.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of G_K → Out(π₁^geom(X)) (Belyi–Matsumoto; Hoshi–Mochizuki for finitely generated fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi 1979 (P¹ minus 3 points), Matsumoto 1996 (affine curves), Hoshi–Mochizuki ~2011 (general hyperbolic curves)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions faithfulness via Belyi for P¹ − {0,1,∞}

ideas.what: Lifting automorphisms of fundamental groupoids to covering groupoids fixing a vertex; non-connected (K-connected) covers.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of outer automorphisms along open subgroups / Galois-equivariant covering theory

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a curve-by-curve characterization of the image of Gal(K̄/K) (K finitely generated over Q) in automorphisms of the fundamental groupoid tower. It uses (a) lifts fixing K-rational points of all covers and (b) stability of images of π₁ under all maps to hyperbolic curves. It thus mixes section-conjecture data (rational points) with I/OM-type morphism compatibility for a single curve rather than for all varieties.
missed.quote: conjecturer que ces conditions sont … draconiennes … que Θ provient bien d'un u ∈ Γ, lorsque X est (disons) courbe algébrique anabélienne, avec K extension de type fini de Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pop's I/OM results work with all varieties or birationally in dimension ≥2. A single-curve version that uses the rational points of all covers as rigidifying data is, to my knowledge, not stated in the literature. It would connect the section conjecture to I/OM-type characterizations, and it predates Ihara's question.

missed.claim: Explicit question whether u is unique when K has positive transcendence degree but is finite over the field of moduli of X.
missed.quote: il faut au moins supposer que le corps modulaire de X a même degré de transcendance … Je ne sais pas si … unicité dans ce cas
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially later settled (I believe) by injectivity results of Hoshi–Mochizuki type for hyperbolic curves over finitely generated fields. It shows Grothendieck identified the field-of-moduli criterion early.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear, early (pre-Esquisse) formulation of a Galois-image characterization conjecture for an individual anabelian curve. It anticipates Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto-type statements and incorporates rational-point (section) data. It also correctly identifies the field-of-moduli condition for faithfulness. Its spirit is known from Esquisse, but this precise form appears unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads '…ment draconiennes [pour] (même … dans la considération des Θ^ν)', continuing 'draconiennes' from p. 94. The superscript insertion near the top right is ambiguous ('nécessaires'/'suffisantes'), but the sense is that the conditions suffice.
Line 4: '[pour impli]quer que Θ provient bien [d'un u] ∈ Γ'.
'dès[?] par[?] pourrait s'attendre' ≈ 'pour qu'on puisse s'attendre à l'unicité de u'.
'd'un groupoïde comme Γ' should be 'comme 𝒞' (script letter, the groupoid Π̂₁(X,I), matching 𝒯̃/𝒞̃ on the next page), not the Galois group Γ.
Margin appears to contain 'Belyi' and 'les conditions algébriques' near the bottom left.
